newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies close limit down, hogs rally late.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies close limit down, hogs rally late.

text.p: CME pork belly futures closed down the daily limit of 2.000 cents per lb across the board in a shortened pre-holiday session. Hog futures rallied late to close mostly higher at the noon CDT close.
February pork bellies remained limit down at 78.050 cents with 400 contracts or more to sell in the pool. The synthetic February option ended down 0.950 cent.

The fourth consecutive limit decline followed the sharp break in cash prices recently with the bearish technical picture adding to losses. Further weakness is expected after the holiday, traders said.
Chartists noted that technicals point to bellies going down to the 72 to 74.50 cent area before finding any support.
"They could go lower than that" one chartist said, noting that many traders have been unable to sell with futures down the limit so many days in a row.

Fresh cash belly prices fell $7 to $11 per cwt Thursday, the lowest price since June 26, and remained weak due to reduced demand and the heavy pace of hog slaughter. Some traders look for cash bellies to go under $70 per cwt before uncovering fresh demand.

Hog futures rallied late to close mostly higher with some buy stops adding to the advance in December. October ran up for a net gain late on commercial support despite being pressured most of the session from fund rolling and mixed selling prompted by recent cash weakness, traders said.

Expectations for next week's cash markets firmed and futures recovered late. Packers will likely need some hogs after the holiday. Expectations for improved pork demand after the Labor Day holiday added to support, they said.
"Cash has gotten cheap enough to spark some interest," one trader said.
Pork cutout values fell to lowest levels since July 3 and this may spark renewed demand for products. Product markets typically firm up going into October, they added.
Rand Financials notably bought October late while Chicago Corp and locals lifted December into by stops. Prudential spread long December/short October early, pit sources said.
In hog options, Lind-Waldock bought February 72 puts, pit sources added.
Hog futures ended up 0.400 to off 0.175 cent with October up 0.025 at 52.425 cents.
